svg.aria-label: Drop no-op proof and termination: the Rust probe writes a value, drops a type whose destructor loops forever, then writes a second value. Main erased the destructor call, so the PTX stored the second value and returned. The PR keeps the call: the PTX stores the first value and spins. A strip explains the three proof states Unseen, InProgress and Proven on a looping destructor and on a diamond that joins back.

text.style: font: 600 17px var(--sans); fill: var(--fg); white-space: pre

svg.text: A destructor that never returns is not a no-op

text.style: font: 400 12.5px var(--sans); fill: var(--muted); white-space: pre

svg.text: cuda-oxide erases a destructor call when a proof says it does nothing visible. The proof now also demands that the destructor returns.
